title: Add operator consent bridge and KMS audit funnel
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: enterprise customers requested an explicit operator consent flow for delegated operator roles and stronger KMS provenance signals in audit logs to satisfy compliance reviews. This PR introduces an operator consent bridge (a lightweight policy and cache that records short-lived operator approvals tied to a tenant and operation signature) and a KMS audit funnel that tags forwarded audit events with provenance headers and a dedupe key to reduce downstream duplication. Key design points: consent entries are scoped to (tenant, operator, action, resource) with TTL and revocation hooks; consent checks are introduced as a middleware early in the request path to avoid expensive KMS calls when denied; KMS audit funnel accepts batched audit payloads, attaches kms_provenance and audit_dedupe_id, and forwards to audit-forwarder service with exponential backoff and idempotency. Backwards compatibility: defaults are disabled via feature flags enable_operator_consent=false and kms_audit_funnel_mode=passthrough. Migration: when enabled, an onboarding job seeds consent cache from operator-approvals table and a one-time audit backfill tags recent events. Checklist: [x] policy model and schema, [x] middleware and cache, [x] KMS header enrichment, [x] audit funnel with dedupe, [x] unit+integration tests, [x] e2e with audit-forwarder in staging, [x] docs + console toggle. Testing plan: unit tests for policy matching, load test for consent cache under 10k req/s, integration test verifying audit envelope includes kms_provenance header, manual compliance review with security team. Related: ENG-1422 and SEC-87 for design review.

merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge. Squash commit message: 'operator(consent): add operator consent bridge and KMS audit funnel — ENG-1422 SEC-87'
release_notes: Adds an operator consent bridge to allow short-lived delegated operator approvals and a KMS audit funnel that enriches forwarded audit records with kms_provenance and dedupe ids. Disabled by default behind feature flags. Config: enable_operator_consent, kms_audit_funnel_mode. See docs/security/operator-consent.md for enablement and migration steps.
security_implications: Introduces additional audit metadata (kms_provenance, audit_dedupe_id) that improves non‑repudiation and reduces duplication. Consent cache stores TTL-limited operator approvals; data stored is tenant+operator+action+resource and is encrypted at rest. KMS headers are HMAC-signed with service KMS key to prevent tampering. Security review completed (SEC-87).
notes_for_ops: When enabling in prod: ramp in stages, monitor consent.cache.hit, audit_forwarder.latency, and audit_forwarder.errors. Recommended rollout: staging -> canary region (10%) -> full. On rollback disable feature flag and purge consent cache if stale entries cause unexpected behavior.
